title: Hip-hop: the birth of a culture
subject: art
description: Born in the Bronx in 1973, hip-hop invents the DJ, rap, breakdancing and graffiti, then conquers the planet.

hero.hook: One block party in the Bronx, and a global culture was born.

blocks.text: Hip-hop is not just a musical genre. It is a culture born out of hardship, in the **Bronx** of New York in the early **1970s**.

In fifty years, a movement invented by young African Americans and Puerto Ricans has transformed records, fashion and language. Here is how a block party became the shared language of young people around the world.

sections.title: The Bronx in ruins and Kool Herc's party

blocks.text: The background was brutal. Between 1950 and 1972, [[Robert Moses's highway policy]] cut through the neighborhood: the [[Cross-Bronx Expressway]], driven by the city planner [[Robert Moses]], destroyed tens of thousands of homes. [[Real estate speculation]] even pushed some landlords to burn their own buildings for the insurance money. People said it plainly: “the Bronx is burning”.

On **August 11, 1973**, at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue, the Jamaican immigrant **Clive Campbell**, known as **Kool DJ Herc**, threw a party in the community room of his building. He invented the *breakbeat*: with two turntables, he isolated and stretched the most danceable rhythmic section of a record. The DJ became a creator, not just someone playing records.

blocks.caption: Kool Herc: two turntables, one break, and hip-hop begins

blocks.text: His “Herculords” sound system was so powerful that he sometimes wired it illegally into the street lamps.

sections.title: Four pillars: DJ, MC, dance, graffiti

blocks.text: Hip-hop organized itself around four disciplines. **DJing** grew sharper with **Grandmaster Flash**, who treated the turntable as an instrument. **MCing** (Master of Ceremonies) turned shout-outs to the crowd into rhythmic poetry: this was the birth of rap.

blocks.caption: Breakdancing and graffiti: the body and the wall as stages

blocks.text: Then came **breakdancing** (B-boying), an athletic dance, and **graffiti**, which turned subway cars into moving galleries. **Afrika Bambaataa**, a former gang member, founded the **Universal Zulu Nation** to replace violence with artistic competition: peace, love, unity and having fun.
[[Scratching]] was born by accident in 1975. **Grand Wizzard Theodore**, aged 12, stopped a record with his hand to hear his mother calling him.

sections.title: From the Bronx to the charts: the commercial explosion

blocks.text: In **1979**, *Rapper's Delight* by the **Sugarhill Gang** proved that rap could be a worldwide hit, even if the pioneers found it too “studio”. In **1982**, *The Message* by **Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five** made the genre a social chronicle of the ghetto.

blocks.caption: Rapper's Delight (1979): rap enters the charts

blocks.text: In the 1990s, the East Coast versus West Coast rivalry shaped the industry. In New York, [[The Notorious B.I.G.]] bet on lyrical virtuosity. In Los Angeles, **N.W.A** and [[Tupac Shakur]] built gangsta rap, which called out police violence. The rapper became an entrepreneur too: labels, clothing, brands.
The loop in *Rapper's Delight* is not a sample. It is a studio re-recording of *Good Times* by Chic, made out of fear of lawsuits.

sections.title: A culture that became a world language

blocks.text: In the 21st century, **Eminem**, **Kanye West** and **Kendrick Lamar** lifted the genre higher. In **2018**, Lamar won a Pulitzer Prize for music, an official honor no rapper had ever received. [[Musical sampling]] has become a universal technique. France is the second biggest rap market in the world.

events.title: Sedgwick Avenue party
events.detail: Kool Herc invents the breakbeat in the Bronx.

blocks.text: Born on August 11, 1973 in the Bronx with Kool Herc, hip-hop went from a local outlet to the most influential culture of our time.
